title: Adaptive Observability Classifier: tenant-aware field encryption, tiered retention, and access audit
creator: Sofia Ramirez
description:
Goal: Implement an adaptive classification and handling pipeline for observability events (traces, logs, metrics metadata) that enforces tenant-aware field-level encryption, tiered retention/eviction policies, and per-role audit trails for access to sensitive payloads. This work enables compliance for regulated customers while preserving queryability for platform debugging (via pseudonymization and reversible encryption for authorized roles).

Scope:
- Classification: lightweight classifier inserted into existing tracing/log ingestion hooks to mark fields as sensitive/confidential/none. Classifier will be config-driven per tenant and extensible via allow-lists/block-lists.
- Field handling: implement field-level pseudonymization (hashing with tenant salt) for low-sensitivity values, and envelope encryption (customer- or platform-managed keys) for high-sensitivity values.
- Retention/eviction: configurable tiered retention windows per tenant and per sensitivity label, with a background archiver that moves long-tail events to encrypted cold storage or deletes them.
- RBAC & audit: integrate with Console's access layer to require explicit RBAC privileges + reason/justification for rehydrating encrypted fields; all rehydration/downloads must produce audit events.
- Compatibility: changes must be backwards-compatible with existing metrics dashboards and tracing tooling (no schema breaks).

Out of scope for this ticket: full UI for per-tenant policy editing (will be separate PM initiative), and on-prem installer changes to HSM integration (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Classifier runs on the ingestion path and tags sensitive fields for at least two sample tenant configs without adding >5ms median ingestion latency
Field-level pseudonymization implemented for strings and identifiers; reversible envelope encryption implemented for fields tagged 'high' sensitivity
Retention policy engine enforces per-tenant windows and successfully moves events older than threshold to encrypted cold storage (test dataset validated)

Access control: attempts to view encrypted fields without the new RBAC flag are denied and generate audit logs; authorized rehydration produces a signed audit event with actor, timestamp and justification
Performance/regression: end-to-end trace ingest and query latency regressions <= 10% on staging compared to baseline; load tests for 10k req/s ingestion run green
E2E tests and unit coverage added; migration/rollback plan documented and dry-run executed in staging
comments: 2025-11-02 - Triage: raised during privacy sprint planning. PM Ana Li prioritized this for regulated-customer onboarding. Initial designs uploaded to Confluence.

2025-11-04 - Design review: agreed on hybrid approach: pseudonymize for most fields, envelope-encrypt only when tenant config requires. Design doc linked. Decision: use tenant-salt for deterministic pseudonyms so we can correlate within a tenant but not across tenants.

2025-11-06 - Eng notes: prototype of classifier implemented as a filter in the trace ingestion pipeline (golang). Local microbenchmarks show +3ms median per trace for a 10-field payload. Need to optimize allocation patterns.

2025-11-08 - Security review (initial): recommend using KMS-backed envelope keys with optional customer-supplied keys. Flagged threat model item: replay attacks on pseudonym mapping service; mitigation: ephemeral HMAC per batch and rate-limited rehydrate API.
2025-11-10 - Blocking: waiting on KMS access contract for customer KMS integration (security/compliance approval). Implementing platform-managed KMS fallback in parallel.
2025-11-12 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4872 - classifier + pseudonymizer implementation. Requests: add more unit tests around unicode and nested JSON fields.

2025-11-14 - Load tests: staging ingestion run at 8k req/s. Observed a 7% median latency increase under load; investigated batching parameters and KV cache interaction. Plan: tune batching window and reuse buffers in next patch.
2025-11-15 - Next steps: finish KMS integration, add RBAC enforcement hooks in console-backend, author migration playbook, and schedule canary rollout for a small tenant group.
